item.title: Serial killer Ted Bundy linked to another Utah girl's cold case murder
item.description: A Utah prosecutor said Ted Bundy was responsible for killing 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith in 1974, a death that had long been listed as a cold case.

item.title: Photos show record-breaking tides flooding homes, roads in California
item.description: Photos show extensive flooding in some parts of Southern California amid record-breaking high tides that have swamped homes and highways.

item.title: No clear winner in Israeli election as polls suggest stalemate
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appears to have won fewer votes than his main challenger, according to early exit polls, but both sides will likely struggle to cobble together a coalition.

item.title: Former election official weighs in on DOJ suit trying to force California to set aside ballots
item.description: A federal judge will rule on a Department of Justice lawsuit seeking to compel California to separate mail ballots from suspected noncitizens. California officials have denounced the lawsuit as a political stunt intended to cast doubt on their election process. Kathy Boockvar, the former Pennsylvania secretary of state, weighs in on this and more.

item.title: Trump backs Paxton in Texas; Rogers repeats Muslim Brotherhood claims against El-Sayed in Michigan
item.description: President Trump rallied for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in Texas. Meanwhile, Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers took aim at opponent Abdul El-Sayed. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi and Aaron Navarro report.

item.title: No official winner yet in Israeli election as votes continue to be counted
item.description: Votes are still being counted in the Israeli election between front-runners Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot with neither likely to obtain a majority. Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: Israel's election results are unclear. Here's what comes next.
item.description: The vote count is still underway in Israel's elections, but no clear winner has emerged. CBS News' Dov Lieber reports.

item.title: At least 64 reported dead in high-speed train crash in Spain
item.description: The number of deaths is expected to rise from the train crash in central Spain, according to a local official.

item.title: High tides break records in California
item.description: Extreme tides, known as "King Tides," are slamming the Southern California coast. Carter Evans reports.

item.title: Trump slams Talarico during Texas rally for Paxton
item.description: President Trump was back in Texas on Tuesday for the third time this month to rally voters, slamming Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico while campaigning for Ken Paxton. Wiejia Jiang and Major Garrett have more.

item.title: Qatari mediators hand Iran new proposal to end the war
item.description: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas after Qatari mediators presented Tehran with a new draft deal to end the war, the Reuters news agency reports.

item.title: Dozens dead as two trains collide in Spain
item.description: A high-speed train crashed into a stopped train in Spain, causing at least 30 deaths. Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: U.S. military strikes alleged drug boat in Pacific, killing 5 people
item.description: The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed by the U.S. military's boat strikes to at least 240 in more than 70 strikes.

item.title: U.S. cruise ship suspends around-the-world voyage due to fuel costs
item.description: The U.S. cruise ship MV Odyssey suspended its three-year, around-the-world voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark.

item.title: At least 30 dead as high-speed train crashes into stopped train in Spain, authorities say
item.description: A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars and killing at least 30 people on Wednesday in central Spain, authorities said.

item.title: Midterm campaigns make final push as early voters hit the polls
item.description: Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, and early voting is underway throughout the country.

item.title: American who was ISIS teen bride convicted of getting weapons training
item.description: Prosecutors said U.S. citizen Halima Salman, now 27, pledged loyalty to the extremist group and willingly participated in its activities.

item.title: Brazil's Flávio Bolsonaro heading for Ecuador, Argentina says
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil's presidential election, was en route to Ecuador after stopping off in Argentina with his family, an Argentine agency said. Earlier, a State Department official told CBS News they would receive U.S. visas.

item.title: Norah's dermatologist shares skin care do's and don'ts
item.description: Dr. Elizabeth Hale​ is an expert on treating damaged skin and shares science-backed advice for looking and feeling your best.

item.title: Do's and Don'ts for Preventing and Reversing Skin Damage
item.description: Norah's dermatologist is back! This week, Dr. Elizabeth Hale discusses the skincare routine that can keep your skin healthy and may also improve wrinkles and reduce skin damage. The two discuss the use of lasers, how menopause accelerates skin aging, and what to eat to help look younger.

item.title: The Secret Story Of Crowning The Sexiest Man Alive
item.description: It started in 1985 with Mel Gibson (by accident), and it has been starting arguments ever since. People Magazine Editor-in-Chief Charlotte Triggs reveals how the Sexiest Man Alive is chosen and what tea she can spill on past winners. Then Vlad and Kelly zoom out: like James Bond, every winner is a mirror of his era, so what does crowning Noah Wyle tell us about 2026 and what it means to be a sexy man? (Sponsored by Casamigos) Before you shake up anything at home, a quick reminder from us: please drink responsibly. And remember, our recipes can be tweaked to make a great mocktail too.

item.title: Classified material missing from Epstein files, documents suggest
item.description: Missing pages and a reference to classified documents contradict the Justice Department's claims about the Epstein files.

item.title: Iran war has cost $47 billion, U.S. military says
item.description: The war with Iran has cost the U.S. military at least $47.1 billion as of mid-October, according to a new estimate from U.S. Central Command obtained by CBS News.

item.title: Alexander brothers sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking
item.description: Alon, Oren and Tal Alexander have been sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking after the trio was convicted of drugging and raping dozens of women.

item.title: Florida mom arrested for allegedly leaving children home alone while on Vegas work trip, police say
item.description: A mother in Florida is under arrest, accused of leaving her four children home alone while she flew to Las Vegas for work. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Grand jury won't indict Cassidy Hutchinson over Jan. 6 testimony
item.description: Federal prosecutors in Washington, D.C., failed to secure an indictment against Cassidy Hutchinson over her testimony about the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot.

item.title: New details revealed in "People's Court" cold case murder arrest
item.description: Michelle Parker went missing on the same day that an episode of "The People's Court" about a dispute between herself and Dale Smith Jr. aired.

item.title: Photos show Ukraine's Starlink was down during fatal strike
item.description: Photos obtained by CBS News show Ukraine's vital connection to Starlink was throttled on Oct. 19, inhibiting its interception capacity when a deadly Russian strike hit a park.

item.title: These factors could decide Netanyahu's fate as Israel votes today
item.description: Israelis are choosing their next government. The race is wide open, and Benjamin Netanyahu's political fate could hinge on a couple key factors.

item.title: 10/25/2026: Destination: Nowhere; #FreeTinaPeters; Australia's Experiment
item.description: First, inside Trump's third-country deportations. Then, Trump, Tina Peters and funds for Colorado. And, Australia's under-16 social media ban.
